dossier.public_summary: The dip looks planet-sized on average, but its depth changes dramatically from sector to sector and from transit to transit, with two very deep events and one missing event in the short 7-transit sample. That level of inconsistency is not expected for a real planet and is best explained by noise or stellar variability rather than a transiting planet.

reasons.why: Depth changes by a factor of ~30 and 3.1% to 0.8%, inconsistent between sectors from the same SPOC source, inconsistent with a single planet transit depth.
reasons.value: p_constant=1.699e-14, sector_depths_by_source verdict=changes_within_a_source, per-sector depths 263+/-609 ppm (21), 2376+/-1019 ppm (47), 8121+/-840 ppm (74), 5900+/-877 ppm (75) vs mean 3636 ppm

reasons.why: Individual transit depths are highly inconsistent, with two very deep events in sectors 74/75 dominating the folded signal and one essentially zero-depth transit, classic for a false alarm/systematics, not for a planet with 7 consistent events.
reasons.value: transits=7, p_consistent=5.738571583310983e-21, top-3 share=0.942, outliers: 11141 ppm sigma=6.4 (epoch 51), 9815 ppm sigma=5.5 (epoch 52), -215 ppm sigma=-4.5 (epoch -54)

reasons.why: No on-target centroid confirmation, but neighbours cannot plausibly reproduce the dip, still does not prove a planet on the target; the sector-dependent and transit-dependent depth changes point to spurious/stellar variability as best explanation.
